neighbours.label: night/bedtime nouns in sleep contexts: ' bed', ' night', ' sleep' ('before bed', 'last night', 'go to sleep'); the - pole is the daytime/morning side ('day', '10 AM', growing up)
fire: I always read a few pages of a novel before bed to help me relax.
She was exhausted because the baby had cried all night.
Try to switch off your phone an hour before you go to sleep.
We stayed up talking until late into the night by the campfire.
He climbed into bed and pulled the blanket over his head.
Did you hear the thunderstorm last night? It kept me awake.
The children were tucked into bed by eight o'clock.
Owls hunt silently through the woods at night.
quiet: I always read a few pages of a novel before lunch to help me relax.
She was exhausted because the baby had cried all afternoon.
Try to switch off your phone an hour before you go to work.
We stayed up talking until the early morning light appeared.
He climbed into the car and pulled the seatbelt across his chest.
Did you hear the thunderstorm this morning? It woke the dog.
The children were dropped at school by eight o'clock.
Hawks hunt across the open fields during the day.

notes: Card + top: ' night' x6, ' bed' x4, ' sleep', also ' December' x6 (cold/dark end of year?). Near misses swap in daytime words in the same frames.
